diagnosis: The scenario fails because the model defaults to high-caution behaviors that satisfy checks without needing private information. Specifically, C2 (linked to PF1) passes in all rollouts because the model assumes a restatement is necessary whenever an accounting error is identified in shared facts. Similarly, C5 (linked to PF3) passes in 75% of rollouts because the model adopts a cautious 'insurance notice' stance as a default safety measure when faced with complex regulatory scenarios.
